AvailabilityCommitment.description:
A contracted availability commitment — capability the battery must HOLD, not may earn.

``committed_power_kw`` is the net-injection capability that must be deliverable on call
throughout every window; ``held_energy_kwh`` is the explicit state-of-energy floor to hold
during windows — ``None`` means no explicit energy hold is contracted, and the consumer
must never invent one. ``tenor_years`` is the contract length from day one; it drives the
closed-form end-of-tenor deliverability check (W7-3: capability at degraded year-N ≥ the
commitment). ``counterparty``/``reference`` carry the contract's provenance — a commitment
with no reference is a modelling input, not evidence, and gates must treat it accordingly.

basis.description: What the assertion rests on, verbatim (e.g. 'owner attestation, on good authority'). None ⇒ the consumer's own default sentence.
basis.title: Basis

committed_power_kw.description: Committed deliverable power (kW) throughout every window.
committed_power_kw.title: Committed Power Kw

confirmed_by.description: Who asserts this commitment exists — a named person for an attestation, a system/record for a transcribed contract. None ⇒ the consumer's own default label.
confirmed_by.title: Confirmed By

counterparty.description: Who the commitment is to (DSO, EMR body, customer).
counterparty.title: Counterparty

held_energy_kwh.description: Explicit state-of-energy floor (kWh) to hold during windows; None = no explicit hold contracted (never defaulted).
held_energy_kwh.title: Held Energy Kwh

reference.description: Contract / tender / agreement id — the commitment's provenance.
reference.title: Reference

stream.description: The value stream this commitment belongs to.

tenor_years.description: Contract length in years from day one; drives the end-of-tenor deliverability check (W7-3).
tenor_years.title: Tenor Years

windows.description: The recurring windows the commitment covers.
windows.title: Windows

AvailabilityCommitment.title: AvailabilityCommitment

AvailabilityWindow.description:
One recurring window in which committed capability must be available.

Market-agnostic calendar shape: optional month and day-of-week filters (``None`` means
every month / every day) plus a same-day ``[start_time, end_time)`` span. An overnight
window (e.g. 23:00–01:00) is expressed as **two** windows — 23:00 to midnight and
midnight to 01:00 — where ``end_time = 00:00`` means the exclusive END of the day
(24:00), so the pre-midnight half is representable (adoption review W7-5). The compiler
maps times onto half-hour indices deterministically (GB local clock, mirroring the DUoS
bands), so the schema itself never needs timezone or wrap logic.

days_of_week.description: Days (0=Monday … 6=Sunday) the window applies to; None = every day.
days_of_week.title: Days Of Week

end_time.description: Window end (exclusive); after start_time, or 00:00 meaning end-of-day.
end_time.title: End Time

label.description: Optional human-readable name, e.g. 'winter evening peak'.
label.title: Label

months.description: Months (1–12) the window applies to; None = all year.
months.title: Months

AvailabilityWindow.title: AvailabilityWindow

BandWindows.description:
When one import-rate band applies, on the same conventions as `WindowedLevy`.

Period-start Europe/London clock, half-open `ClockWindow` s, weekday and weekend as separate
day types, an optional month restriction and sourced non-working ``excluded_dates`` (which fall
to the weekend row). A `BandWindows` with **no window at all** is the residual band, "all other
times"; a stack may carry at most one (`TariffStack._import_rate_windows_consistent`).
BandWindows.title: BandWindows

CdcmTariff.description: A CDCM (LV/HV) tariff: three time bands, fixed, capacity, exceeded capacity, reactive.

exceeded_capacity_p_per_kva_day.title: Exceeded Capacity P Per Kva Day

CdcmTariff.title: CdcmTariff

ClockWindow.description:
A half-open local-clock window ``[start, end)``, quoted as the statements quote it.

Same shape and same conventions as the per-licence-area DUoS band windows a release carries in
``duos.band_windows_by_dno`` (``{start: "16:00", end: "19:00"}``): period-start local clock,
Europe/London, half-open so 19:00 is out of a 16:00–19:00 window. Deliberately NOT a pair of
integers — real published windows land on half-hours (16:30, 19:30) that hour pairs cannot say.
ClockWindow.title: ClockWindow

How much weight a validation result can carry. Ordered worst to best.

(`docs/validation_requirements.md` §2). Defined here rather than in `gridq.quotes.confidence`
so the band and the Gate-2 ceiling can be **persisted on the QuoteRecord** and enforced by the
lifecycle gate (N21); `gridq.quotes.confidence` re-exports it, so its public name is unchanged.

DerivedAssumption.description:
One recorded stand-in for a missing input, and everything needed to judge and confirm it.

Carried on `SiteModel.derived_assumptions` when the value was derived **offline** and actually
consumed by the run (it enters ``input_hash``, so two runs on different derived capacities can
never share a ``run_id``), and emitted transiently by the ingestion gates when a run continued
past a missing input without a recorded value (those reach the quote's warnings and the
confidence factors, never the site — a gate observation is not an input and must not move any
existing run identity).

**Immutable (``frozen``).** The record is part of the run's identity, so it must not be able to
change after the validator has passed it: ``rec.kind = "pending_permission"`` on a record that
already carries a value would flip `report_label` to *"requires customer consent"* and produce
exactly the record `_enforce_class_and_ceiling` refuses to build. Only this model is frozen —
`GridQModel` cannot be (`gridq.schemas.provenance`).
DerivedAssumption.title: DerivedAssumption

One IC-4 evidence object, by hash, and what it supports on the record that carries it.

``supports`` names the thing evidenced: a chassis field path (``connection.mic_kw``), a
revenue stream id, or a registered extension id. The reference says a document exists and
which one; whether it is valid, third-party and in scope is decided where the object is in
hand (`gridq.contracts.evidence.resolve_ref`, `assess`), never here.
EvidenceLink.title: EvidenceLink

ExportArrangement.description:
A site's declared export / route-to-market arrangement.

``route`` defaults to ``ExportRoute.UNKNOWN`` — the honest state until the arrangement is
evidenced. Nothing here is estimated by the engine; a missing value stays ``None`` and
becomes a ranked data-ask upstream, never an invented number.

aggregator_cut_pct.description: The aggregator / route-to-market take on gross flexibility/export revenue, as a fraction in [0, 1]. A per-site override of the assumption default (local_flex_piclo.aggregator_cut_pct); None = fall back to the assumption default.
aggregator_cut_pct.title: Aggregator Cut Pct

counterparty.description: Who the export / route-to-market arrangement is with (a PPA offtaker or a flexibility aggregator); None when unknown or not applicable.
counterparty.title: Counterparty

export_tariff_gbp_per_kwh.description: Declared export tariff (£/kWh) under a PPA / export arrangement; None when unknown or not applicable.
export_tariff_gbp_per_kwh.title: Export Tariff Gbp Per Kwh

local_flex_agreed_rate_gbp_per_mwh.description: Declared agreed local-flexibility rate (£/MWh) under a flexibility-aggregator arrangement, when one has been agreed; None when unknown or not applicable. Additive, None default (issue 018 / D8) - recorded verbatim, priced by a later WS-C slice; nothing here is estimated by the engine.
local_flex_agreed_rate_gbp_per_mwh.title: Local Flex Agreed Rate Gbp Per Mwh

How a site's exported / flexible energy reaches a market (route-to-market).

Recorded on the ``ExportArrangement`` *model* (``export_arrangement.py``). ``UNKNOWN`` is
the honest default until the arrangement is evidenced; ``NONE`` means the site deliberately
has no export / route-to-market. This vocabulary prices nothing — it is a data contract only.

ProvisioningRequirement.description:
A declared obligation to serve load the connection cannot deliver in a window.

``additional_load_kw`` is NEW demand the customer states the site needs inside the
windows (demand the meter has never seen — a declared fact with the requirement as its
provenance). ``serve_metered_shortfall`` covers the case the meter *does* show: observed
load riding at/over the import cap (clipped demand). At least one must be active or the
requirement demands nothing. When both apply the shortfall is physically joint — the
battery covers ``max(0, total − cap)``; it cannot serve the addition while leaving the
metered excess unserved.

``import_cap_kw`` is the window-effective deliverable import; ``None`` means the site's
own ``max_import_kw`` applies (the consumer resolves it — never defaulted here).
``declared_counterfactual_gbp_per_year`` is the customer's stated cost of the alternative
and the ONLY £ input this product introduces; ``counterfactual_basis`` (what the figure
is, verbatim) is mandatory alongside it. A requirement with no ``reference`` is a
modelling input, not evidence — gates must treat it accordingly (W7-4).

additional_load_kw.description: Declared NEW demand (kW, flat within windows) the connection cannot deliver; None = no new load declared.
additional_load_kw.title: Additional Load Kw

additional_load_profile_daily_kw.description: Declared NEW demand as a manual half-hourly daily curve entered from the outside (48 kW values, slot 0 = 00:00 local; applied inside windows on the days/months the windows cover). Mutually exclusive with additional_load_kw (D42). A full declared series file ref is the v2 shape.
additional_load_profile_daily_kw.title: Additional Load Profile Daily Kw

counterfactual_basis.description: What the declared counterfactual is, verbatim (e.g. 'NGED reinforcement quote ref …, annualised over …'). Mandatory alongside the £ figure.
counterfactual_basis.title: Counterfactual Basis

counterparty.description: Who the obligation is to (normally the site customer).
counterparty.title: Counterparty

declared_counterfactual_gbp_per_year.description: Customer-declared annual cost of the alternative (DNO reinforcement, genset, lost production). Never estimated by the engine; absent = the stream prices £0 and only the engine-measured opportunity cost is reported.
declared_counterfactual_gbp_per_year.title: Declared Counterfactual Gbp Per Year

import_cap_kw.description: Window-effective deliverable import (kW); None = the site's max_import_kw applies (resolved by the consumer, never defaulted here).
import_cap_kw.title: Import Cap Kw

reference.description: Contract / agreement id — the obligation's provenance; required before any FIRM treatment.
reference.title: Reference

serve_metered_shortfall.description: Also cover the metered load's own excess over the import cap (clipped-demand case).
serve_metered_shortfall.title: Serve Metered Shortfall

tenor_years.description: Obligation length in years from day one; drives the end-of-tenor floors (W7-3 closed form).
tenor_years.title: Tenor Years

windows.description: The recurring windows the obligation covers.
windows.title: Windows

ProvisioningRequirement.title: ProvisioningRequirement

RateUnit.description:
The unit a commercially agreed rate is expressed in.

Exists because `agreed_rate_gbp` was a bare float that different downstream code paths read
as four incompatible units (hostile review F-17). £/kWh and £/MW/yr differ by six orders of
magnitude, so an unlabelled number is not a rate — it is a guess waiting to be made.
RateUnit.title: RateUnit

RevenueStreamConsent.description: Explicit customer authorisation to pursue ONE revenue stream, captured at intake.

agreed_rate_gbp.description: An optional commercially agreed rate, verbatim, for streams whose agreed rate is not already held elsewhere on the SiteModel. MUST be accompanied by `agreed_rate_unit` — the number alone is meaningless. None when the stream needs no such rate or none was supplied. The export tariff / aggregator cut / local-flex rate live on ExportArrangement and are not duplicated here.
agreed_rate_gbp.title: Agreed Rate Gbp

agreed_rate_unit.description: The unit `agreed_rate_gbp` is expressed in. REQUIRED whenever a rate is given (hostile review F-17): this field was previously a bare, unit-less float that downstream code read as £/kWh, £/MWh, £/kW/yr AND £/MW/yr depending on the stream. A single mis-united intake entry therefore produced contracted floor revenue wrong by up to three orders of magnitude, and the record still validated cleanly.

consented.description: True iff the customer explicitly consented, at intake, to GridQ pursuing this revenue stream on their behalf.
consented.title: Consented

notes.description: Free-text notes on the consent / agreed rate (verbatim).
notes.title: Notes

RevenueStreamConsent.title: RevenueStreamConsent

SupplyBoundary.title: SupplyBoundary

TariffBasis.description:
What the stack's rates include (D103). Required on every `TariffStack`.

``vat`` says whether the £ figures include VAT; ``vat_rate_fraction`` is the rate that was
included (required when ``vat="included"``, refused when ``"excluded"``) and is read from the
record, never from a release key or from memory. ``vat_attestation`` says how the VAT basis is
known: ``stated_by_record`` (the invoice or the record's author states it) or ``derived``
(inferred under H-01, which then needs a `DerivedAssumption` on ``tariff_stack.basis.vat`` on
the same site, enforced by `SiteModel`). ``levies`` and ``network_charges`` say whether those
lines are itemised in this stack or already sit inside the unit rates, or (network only) are
not charged at all, as on a private-wire supply.
TariffBasis.title: TariffBasis

TariffProvenance.description:
Where each component of the stack came from (D104). Required on every stack.

``own_invoice``: the site's own invoiced rate. ``published_for_site``: the DNO's published rate
for the site's own licence area, voltage and band. ``by_analogy``: another site's or another
tariff's rate. ``assumed``: constructed or assumed. ``not_charged``: the component is not
charged to this site (private wire). Only the first two and the last are the site's own.
TariffProvenance.title: TariffProvenance

TariffStack.description:
Import/export rates, DUoS bands and levy lines for a site.

``import_rates`` / ``export_rates`` / ``levies`` map a label (e.g. ``"red"``, ``"RO"``)
to a £/kWh value. Rates are non-negative (£/kWh).

capacity_charge_gbp_per_kva_day.title: Capacity Charge Gbp Per Kva Day

TariffStack.title: TariffStack

WindowedLevy.description:
A £/kWh levy line charged **only inside a stated time window**, not on every half-hour.

**Why the type exists.** ``TariffStack.levies`` is a flat ``{label: £/kWh}`` map and every
consumer sums it and applies the total to all 17,520 half-hours. That is right for CCL, RO,
CfD, BSUoS, AAHEDC and Nuclear RAB — all of which bite on boundary import across the whole
year — and **wrong for the Capacity Market supplier obligation**, which GB suppliers charge on
peak-window consumption only ("Obligation Costs … are charged on consumption during the winter
peak period; from 16:00 and 19:00 on working days between November & February", npower Business
Solutions). Put a 30 p/kWh Capacity Market line in the flat map and the objective charges it on
every charged kWh at 03:00 in July, which would wreck the dispatch. So a windowed levy is its
own field with its own calendar, and the flat map keeps meaning exactly what it meant.

**The window is expressed the way the DUoS band windows are** (`ClockWindow`, period-start
Europe/London clock, half-open, weekday and weekend as separate day types, an optional month
restriction), and `gridq.optimisation.tariff_calendar` bands it with the same machinery it
bands DUoS with — one set of conventions, not two.

``excluded_dates`` carries the **non-working days** inside the window's months. It is required
for honesty rather than precision: the Capacity Market window is "working days", GB bank
holidays fall Monday–Friday, and ``dayofweek < 5`` alone would charge Christmas Day as a
working day and **overstate** the avoided cost by roughly one working day in 28. The dates are
sourced (gov.uk's published bank-holiday list), never derived from a rule — leaving it empty is
permitted and is disclosed as an overstatement, never silently assumed harmless.
WindowedLevy.title: WindowedLevy
